title: The Seven Kings
objective: After this level you can outline Rome’s age of kings and how kingship worked there.
summary: Seven kings ruled from 753 to 509 BCE, each chosen with the Senate’s and people’s approval. Numa founded religion; Servius, the census.

cards.headline: Before consuls and emperors, Rome had kings. Seven, if you trust the legends.
Seven kings
cards.body: Roman tradition counted seven kings, from Romulus in 753 BCE to Tarquin the Proud, driven out in 509 BCE. Kingship was not simply passed from father to son: each king was said to be chosen with the approval of the Senate and the people.

cards.headline: Remembered for different things
cards.body: Numa Pompilius, the second king, was remembered as the founder of Rome’s religion and calendar. Servius Tullius, the sixth, was credited with the first census, which sorted citizens by wealth. Legends like these explained where Roman institutions came from.

cards.fact: The Senate started as the king’s advisers.
cards.context: It began as a council of elders who counseled the king. It would long outlast the kings themselves.

questions.prompt: From Level 5: what did tradition say Rome’s last three kings had in common?
questions.explanation: Roman tradition held that the last three kings were Etruscans, a sign of Etruscan influence.
